subject: Career
title: Cross-Functional Relationships
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cross-Functional Relationships.

hook.text: The engineer who knows the sales team. The marketer who understands finance. Cross-functional people are gold.

buildup.text: Organizations are siloed by design. Information flows vertically within teams, not horizontally across them.

discovery.text: People who bridge silos see the full picture. They spot opportunities and solve problems others can't.

twist.text: Cross-functional work is often unrewarded in formal reviews — but it's the #1 factor in leadership selection.

climax.text: Volunteer for cross-functional projects. Attend other teams' demos. Learn their language.

punchline.text: The view from between teams is the leadership view.

quiz.question: Why are cross-functional relationships valuable for career growth?
options: They provide the full-picture view needed for leadership
They look good on a resume

details.summary: Cross-functional relationships connect you to colleagues in departments outside your own, providing broader organizational perspective and access to resources, information, and opportunities that siloed professionals miss.
details.whyItMatters: Career advancement increasingly requires cross-functional visibility. Leaders who understand finance, operations, marketing, and engineering through personal relationships make better strategic decisions.
takeaways: Volunteer for cross-functional projects to build natural relationships
Understand each function's priorities and speak their language
Cross-functional allies help you navigate organizational politics

faq.question: How do you build relationships with people in departments you never interact with?
faq.answer: Request brief informational meetings to understand their function's challenges and priorities. Offer to share how your department's work affects theirs. Internal lunch-and-learn sessions and cross-functional project teams are also natural relationship builders.

faq.question: Why are cross-functional relationships important for getting promoted?
faq.answer: Promotion decisions at senior levels involve input from multiple departments. Having advocates across functions ensures your name comes up positively in conversations you are not part of. Cross-functional visibility also demonstrates the organizational thinking leaders need.
